subject: Proposal: auto-renew opt-in + termination fallback compromise
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@valleycloud.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@valleycloud.com
Date: Wed, 03 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ValleyCloud markups: auto-renew & termination concerns
Attachments: ValleyCloud_Redlines_MSA_v1.pdf (pdf)

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking the time to talk yesterday. Attached are our markup notes on the MSA and order form. Two quick flag items before we dig into redlines:

- Auto-renew: we are not comfortable with automatic renewal without an explicit opt-in checkbox for pilot/POC accounts. For enterprise contracts, auto-renew can work but we need a 60-day notice window.
- Termination for convenience (TFC): ValleyCloud accepts TFC but requests a 90-day notice and a phased refund for any pre-paid committed fees if termination occurs within the first 12 months.

We put comments in the attached PDF where the contract language is ambiguous. Can you confirm whether Redwood would consider: (a) enabling an opt-in toggle on the order form for pilots, and (b) offering a two-tier notice (45 days for standard customers, 90 days for enterprise)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround on this — procurement is trying to hit their executive review next week.

Best,
Maya Singh
Sr. Procurement Manager | ValleyCloud Inc.
maya@valleycloud.com

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@valleycloud.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ValleyCloud markups: auto-renew & termination concerns
Attachments: Redwood_MSA_v3_suggested_changes.docx (docx)

Maya — thanks, received and reviewed the highlights. Short answers up front: yes on an order-form opt-in model for pilots (we can implement an explicit toggle and label it "pilot auto-renew opt-in") and we can consider differentiated notice windows.

Next steps from Redwood:
- I'll loop in Legal (cc'd) to draft alternative language for the termination-for-convenience section that attempts to bridge your 90-day request and our preferred 45/60 structure.
- Internal ask: can you share which customers ValleyCloud classifies as "enterprise" for this deal (budget threshold or seat count)? That helps us decide whether to default to 45 or 90 days in our templates.

I'll attach our suggested changes so legal can redline in-place. If procurement is under time pressure, we can propose a compromise and include a short escalation clause to revisit after the first 12 months. Thoughts?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 04 Feb 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: RE: ValleyCloud markups: suggested language and fallback options

Grace / Laura / Aditya — internal legal take (high level) below. I drafted snippets we can propose back to ValleyCloud; feel free to reuse.

Summary positions:
- Auto-renew: Accept opt-in for pilots. For billed/committed customers, we prefer automatic renewal with 45-day notice for standard accounts and 90-day for enterprise — but we can be flexible on initial deals.
- Termination for convenience: Agree to permit TFC, subject to (i) a 60-day notice period for all customers by default, and (ii) pro-rata refund for pre-paid amounts where termination happens mid-cycle. For early-termination within first 12 months, we recommend a capped termination fee equal to 25% of remaining committed fees to protect revenue.

Suggested redline snippets (place into Section 5.2 — Termination for Convenience):
- "Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to Redwood. If Customer terminates within the first twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, Customer shall pay a termination fee equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of the remaining committed fees for the then-current Term, except that Redwood shall provide a pro-rata refund for any pre-paid but unused fees."

- Order Form opt-in language for pilots (Order Form worksheet):
  "Pilot Auto-Renew Opt-In: By checking this box, Customer elects to enable automatic renewal at the end of the pilot term. If left unchecked, the pilot term will expire without automatic renewal and Customer's account will enter non-billable state until a new Order Form is executed."

Operational notes:
- We should add an internal flag on new POC orders: "pilot_auto_renew_allowed" and route billing to pegged workflows. Engineering can implement a UI toggle if Product agrees.

I'll prepare a tracked-change version if you want to send this to ValleyCloud later today.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Policy | Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya@valleycloud.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@valleycloud.com
Date: Thu, 04 Feb 2027 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ValleyCloud markups: auto-renew & termination concerns
Attachments: ValleyCloud_Redlines_MSA_v2.pdf (pdf)

Grace / team — thanks for the quick internal coordination and the language proposals. Procurement and Legal talked it over and ValleyCloud can move on the following: 

- Pilot auto-renew: Accept Redwood's opt-in checkbox approach — thanks for proposing that.
- Notice windows: ValleyCloud is willing to accept 45 days for SMB/standard accounts but insists on 90 days for Enterprise classified accounts (they define enterprise as annual spend > $250k or > 500 seats).
- TFC: We are not comfortable with a flat 25% termination fee for early exits. Our counterproposal: allow TFC with a phased refund schedule for pre-paid fees and require a 90-day notice if termination occurs within the first 12 months. For terminations after 12 months, a 60-day notice is acceptable.

Attached is an updated PDF with inline comments. Two asks for Redwood: (1) confirm the enterprise spend threshold above, and (2) replace the proposed 25% flat fee with a pro-rata refund schedule in your next redline.

Best,
Maya

Maya — thanks for the clear counterproposal and for the quick turnaround. We can live with your enterprise definition (annual spend > $250k or >500 seats). To close this round, Redwood proposes the following compromise so we can move to signature: 

1) Notice windows:
   - SMB / Standard accounts: forty-five (45) days' prior written notice to terminate for convenience.
   - Enterprise accounts (as defined by ValleyCloud above): ninety (90) days' prior written notice to terminate for convenience.

2) Termination for convenience & refunds/fees:
   - If Customer terminates within the first twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, Customer may terminate for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice and Redwood will provide a pro-rata refund for any pre-paid, unused fees. No additional early termination fee will be charged as long as the sixty (60) day notice requirement is met.
   - If Customer terminates after the first twelve (12) months, Customer may terminate for convenience upon the notice period applicable to their account tier (45 or 90 days) with a pro-rata refund for pre-paid, unused fees.

3) Pilot Auto-Renew Opt-In:
   - Redwood will add an explicit checkbox on the pilot/POC order form labeled "Pilot Auto-Renew Opt-In." If unchecked, pilot terms will expire at the end of the pilot unless a new Order Form is executed.

4) Review cadence & escalation:
   - Both parties agree to a 30-day operational review after go-live for pilot accounts to ensure billing toggles and entitlement flags are working. Any unexpected billing impacts will be resolved through a joint escalation path to DRM (billing ops) and ValleyCloud procurement.

If that is acceptable, we'll send a tracked-change MSA and a DocuSign packet. If ValleyCloud prefers the earlier ValleyCloud counter (90-day early termination within first 12 months), we can add a limited carveout for pre-paid subscriptions > $500k spend to require 90 days instead of 60.

Please confirm and I'll send the DocuSign link and the redlined doc for legal sign-off.

Best regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
